name: Rafael Sloan
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember the first load I guided without looking at my feet.” People around the bank steps know Rafael by a small Monday habit. Rafael takes a few minutes to read the public notices, especially the ones written in a hurry.
voice: I spent my first year here looking down. This gull was the first thing that made me look up.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a pale blue work shirt and a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light. Rafael has a wide brow and a narrow jaw, with short black hair swept back. Rafael folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing during a conversation.
personality: Rafael has a long memory for unfair prices and a short one for small insults. Rafael can get along perfectly well with an enemy provided the account between them is clear.
agenda: To learn which movements make the crane shadow change.
family: Douglas Waters is Rafael’s cousin raised in the same household. Rafael brings a spare shopping bag. Douglas chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The release address*, Douglas says, “I rented his old room. The first letter that arrived asked my permission to send another.”
connections: Ana Powell. A parent waiting through another spring finds company in a new worker learning to look up.

reactions.situation: A visitor reaches the quay too late to see it
reactions.response: Rafael shows the visitor where the shadow fell and when the next chance comes.

reactions.situation: An argument on the pavement makes a bystander feel unsafe
reactions.response: Rafael walks with the bystander to a staffed doorway and checks whether they want someone called.
